patch_description: The current algorithm routes each partition of each destination independently with only intra-destination congestion awareness, paying full cost on every edge for every partition. Since this is a broadcast (multicast) problem, edges already used by a prior destination's route can carry additional traffic at near-zero marginal cost. The best-performing prior generations (1035→1025 costs) showed that candidate selection and per-partition spreading help, but none combined (a) cross-destination edge reuse via a Steiner-tree-style heuristic with (b) per-partition load spreading. I implement a shortest-path-union Steiner heuristic: maintain a working "tree" graph whose edges, once paid for by any destination, cost a small epsilon for all subsequent destinations and partitions. Each partition of each destination runs Dijkstra on this reduced-cost working copy; since tree edges are nearly free, later destinations naturally route through the existing broadcast tree instead of paying for fresh parallel links, eliminating redundant transfers. After routing, each used edge's cost in the working copy drops to epsilon, so the union of paths approximates a directed Steiner tree. Edges are still emitted exactly as `[s, t, G[s][t]]` via `append_dst_partition_path`, and the original G/h are never mutated, avoiding the fatal failure modes of earlier generations. The per-partition load counter is retained (with a mild congestion penalty on the working copy) so the num_partitions copies of each partition still spread across parallel paths when beneficial.
